correctness.rationale: The quotient H^0(Q,O(2)) has 511 nonzero sections. Enumerating the full 120-element stabilizer produces 17 orbits, with exact four-chart Jacobian Gröbner checks showing precisely five smooth orbits (60,30,60,30,60). A separately programmed lex-Gröbner test on all 511 sections reproduces 240 smooth sections and point counts (1:60,2:90,3:60,4:30). The independent rank-five evaluation and 15 secant-plane-pair argument prove that every section through all five rational Q-points is reducible and singular. Adjunction gives genus one and degree four.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither characteristic-zero Segre-symbol theory nor existence of pencils of smooth members implies the exact count and orbit splitting of all anticanonical divisors on the nonsplit F2 quadric. The base curve of a pair of quadrics may be smooth even when one of the other rational members is singular; hence restricting to all-smooth pencils is not broader coverage.

value.rationale: The anticanonical system on the unique nonsplit rational quadric over F2 is a natural and geometrically distinguished moduli slice. The complete five embedded orbit types, full rational-point distribution, and sharp exclusion of the Hasse-permitted five-point case are motivated geometric classifications. The exclusion additionally has a simple intrinsic ovoid/secant-plane decomposition proof and cannot be inferred solely from counts of all-smooth pencils.
